1.
The present claim petition is filed under section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 by the petitioner seeking compensation on account of the death of her husband in a road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts, as narrated by the petitioner in the claim petition as well as in the FIR, are that on 30.11.2019 at about 6:30 pm, the deceased was travelling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing registration No. DL-5S4-4048, which was being driven by Shyam Giri and when they reached near village Baadi, Police Station- Hasayan, Hathras, U.P., the offending vehicle bearing registration No.
UP-82AF-2112, being driven by respondent No.1 at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner, hit the vehicle of the deceased.
It is further stated that the deceased sustained injuries in the accident and was admitted in the hospital where he later succumbed to his injuries during treatment.
In connection with said accident, FIR No. 0237/19 under Section 279/337/338/304A IPC, was registered at Police Station- Hasayan and Respondent No.1 was charge-sheeted after investigation.

sentences.text: After service of notice, both the respondents entered appearance and filed their separate written statements.

4. Respondent No.1 filed his written statement, stating therein that petition is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed as it is without any substance and discloses no cause of action against him.
It is further stated that the assertions made by the petitioner are false, frivolous and devoid of merits.
Respondent No.1 further stated in the written statement that the accident in question did not occur due to his vehicle and that he has been wrongly impleaded in the present matter.

It is further stated by respondent No.1 that he is the driver-cum-owner of the vehicle bearing Registration No.UP-82AF-2112, that he was holding a valid and effective driving licence on the date of accident,
and that the said vehicle was duly insured on the relevant date.
The remaining averments of the claim petition have been specifically denied by the respondent No.1.
5. Respondent No. 2 - insurer has filed its written statement and raised the objection that the present case is beyond the territorial jurisdiction of this Tribunal.
It is further stated that the accident in question was a head-on-collision and that the deceased himself was driving his vehicle in a negligent manner.
It is further stated that since the accident was a head-on-collision between two vehicles, the insurer of the second vehicle was also a necessary party to the present proceedings.
It is further stated that the FIR was lodged after a delay of four days and that the FIR was initially lodged against an unknown vehicle.
Other general defences have also been taken by the insurance company.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the following issues were framed on 29.08.2023:

(i). Whether Har Charan Giri, husband of the petitioner died in a motor vehicular accident which occurred on 30.11.2019 at 6:30 p.m., near village Baadi, Hasayan,
Hathras, U.P., within jurisdiction of PS Hasayan, U.P. due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle bearing Registration No.UP-82AF-2112, driven by Respondent No.1 / Satendra Pal?

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation on account of the said death, and if so, to what extent and from whom?(OPP)
(iii) Relief.

The aforesaid issues are decided as under:
ISSUE No. 1 :
Whether Har Charan Giri, husband of the petitioner died in a motor vehicular accident which occurred on 30.11.2019 at 6:30 p.m., near village Baadi, Hasayan,
Hathras, U.P., within jurisdiction of PS Hasayan, U.P. due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle bearing Registration No.UP-82AF-2112, driven by Respondent No.1 / Satendra Pal? (OPP)
13.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as that required in criminal trials.
The applicable test is that of preponderance of probabilities, which governs civil proceedings.
It is also well- settled that the Claim Tribunal is not bound by the strict and technical rules of evidence.

Further, while conducting an inquiry under Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act,
the Claims Tribunal may adopt such summary procedure as it deems fit.
14.
In order to prove her case, petitioner being wife of the deceased examined herself as PW1.

Further, the eye-witness Sh.Praveen Kumar was examined as PW2, who clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief that on 30.11.2019 at about 6:30 pm, when he was returning from Purdil Nagar to his residence after attending marriage and when he reached near the accident spot at Village Baadi, Police Station Hasayan, Hathras, U.P., he saw that the deceased Harcharan Giri was riding on a motorcycle as a pillion rider.

He further deposed that respondent No. 1 while driving the vehicle bearing registration No.UP-82AF-2112 at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner hit the motorcycle of the deceased from the front side.
He further deposed that due to the said impact both persons Shyam Lal and deceased Harcharan Giri fell down on the road and sustained multiple injuries, thereafter they were taken to the Hospital.
He also deposed that respondent No.1 fled away from the spot after the accident.
He categorically stated that the accident occurred due to the rash & negligence of respondent No.1.
During his cross-examination, he disclosed that the number of the offending vehicle was mentioned in his statement recorded by the police.

He further deposed that the deceased was not related to him; however, he and the deceased Ramvati vs Satendra Pal And Others on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63500476/
3 were the residents of the same village.

sentences.text: He denied the suggestion that he was an implanted or interested witness introduced for the purpose of enabling the petitioner to obtain compensation.
There is no reason to doubt the testimony of PW2, and his testimony remained intact during cross-examination.
He was not cross- examined by respondent No.1.
No suggestion was put to PW2 that respondent No.1 was not driving the offending vehicle at the date and time of accident.
No suggestion was also given to PW2 that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident or that it had not fled from the spot after the accident.
It is seen that PW2 is a witness cited in the charge-sheet.
The FIR was lodged without any inordinate delay.
A bare perusal of the charge-sheet further reveals that after investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against Respondent no. 1- Satender Pal as the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Filing of the charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle prima-facie points towards his culpability.
R-1 has not disputed that after investigation, charge-sheet was filed against him.
It is not the case that Respondent No.1 & 2 have filed any complaint to Higher Authority for their false implication in the present matter.
(In this context reliance is placed on the case of New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

sentences.text: If any party do not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
16. The respondent no.1 is the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle, he did not lead any evidence to prove anything contrary to the claim of the petitioners.

Hence, it is required to cite the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3)
AD Delhi 310, wherein it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.

18. Thus, in view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioners have been able to prove that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle by Respondent no.1, which resulted in fatal injuries to the deceased Harcharan Giri.
Therefore, issue no.1 is decided in favour of the petitioners.
19. In view of the finding on issue no.1, the petitioner is entitled to compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still remains to be adjudicated.

20.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 21.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 mandates the Claims Tribunal to conduct an inquiry and to determine an amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.
While assessing the compensation, the Tribunal must ensure that the award is neither a windfall nor a pittance, but a fair recompense for the injuries suffered.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).

22. In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.
(2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

sentences.text: 19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps: death case Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier) death case
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)
The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand) when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."
24.

Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:
PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
(A). Age of deceased :
25.
As per the Aadhar card of the deceased which is Ex.PW1/8, the age of the deceased is 59 years and 10 months on the date of accident.
Thus, his age is taken to be 59 years 10 months at the time of accident.

(B). Assessment of Income of deceased :
26.
PW1 stated in her testimony that the deceased was working as Home Guard in U.P. Government and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
However, PW1 has neither placed on record or proved any salary slip / employment document to establish the income of the deceased.
No witness has been examined from the employer of the deceased.

sentences.text: employment of the deceased was with the government or a private sector.
PW1 has relied upon Identity card of the deceased issued by the Uttar Pradesh Homeguard; however the said document does not mentions the date of service and salary details.
Admittedly, no document in support of the education or income of the deceased has been filed on record.
As per Aadhar Card, the deceased was a resident of Uttar Pradesh.

No identity document has been filed to suggest that the deceased was residing and working in Delhi at the time of accident and further in FIR and medical document,
there is nothing to suggest that the deceased was a resident of Delhi.

Hence, in the considered view of this Tribunal, the income of the deceased is required to be assessed as per the minimum wages of an unskilled worker applicable in Uttar Pradesh, which were Rs.8278/- per month at the time of accident.
Thus, the income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.8,278/- per month.

(C). Number of dependents :
27.
The present claim petition has been filed by the wife of the deceased.
The children of the deceased are stated to be major and not dependent up him.
Therefore, for the purpose of assessing dependency, the wife of the deceased alone is considered to be the dependents.

(D). Application of Multiplier:
28.
As discussed above, the deceased is considered to be 59 years and 10 months of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

(E). Future Prospects:
30.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
(iv) In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
31. The deceased can be considered a self-employed / on fixed salary, in absence of any documentary evidence to establish a permanent job or regular increase in income.

In view of the aforesaid, the deceased, who was aged 59 years and 10 months at the time of the accident, is entitled to an addition of 10% to his income towards future prospects in terms of the decision of the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court of India in the case, National Insurance Company Ltd. 32.
After determining the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions are required to be made from the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses and living expenses.

Deductions out of earning of the Number of deceased dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six)

(G). NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
35.

In the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed toward loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.
The date of accident is 03.11.2019.

Accordingly, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively towards loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is liable to be awarded.

Further, in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020,
loss of consortium is payable to each of the legal representatives.

INTEREST ON AWARD:
37.
The petitioner has been pursing the present claim petition since the year 2021.
Accordingly, the petitioner shall also be entitled to interest @ 7.5% per annum on the awarded amount from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.

LIABILITY:
38.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
The insurance company has a contractual as well as statutory liability to indemnify the insured.
In the present case, the insurance company has failed to prove that any term or condition of the insurance policy was breached or violated by the insured.
Therefore, respondent no.2 i.e. the National Insurance Company Ltd is held liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.
39. In view of above discussion, the respondent No. 2- insurer is directed to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hathras, U.P., within jurisdiction of PS Hasayan, U.P. due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle bearing Registration No.UP-82AF-2112, driven by Respondent No.1 / Satendra Pal?
(OPP)

The aforesaid issues are decided as under:
ISSUE No. 1 :
Whether Har Charan Giri, husband of the petitioner died in a motor vehicular accident which occurred on 30.11.2019 at 6:30 p.m., near village Baadi, Hasayan,
Hathras, U.P., within jurisdiction of PS Hasayan, U.P. due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle bearing Registration No.UP-82AF-2112, driven by Respondent No.1 / Satendra Pal? (OPP)
13.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation on account of the said death,
and if so, to what extent and from whom?(OPP)
20.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as that required in criminal trials.
The applicable test is that of preponderance of probabilities, which governs civil proceedings.
It is also well- settled that the Claim Tribunal is not bound by the strict and technical rules of evidence.
Further, while conducting an inquiry under Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act,
the Claims Tribunal may adopt such summary procedure as it deems fit.
14.
In order to prove her case, petitioner being wife of the deceased examined herself as PW1.
A bare perusal of the charge-sheet further reveals that after investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against Respondent no. 1- Satender Pal as the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Filing of the charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle prima-facie points towards his culpability.
(In this context reliance is placed on the case of New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).
If any party do not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.
If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
18. Thus, in view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioners have been able to prove that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle by Respondent no.1, which resulted in fatal injuries to the deceased Harcharan Giri.
These issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are:
(i) additions/ deductions to be made for arriving at the income;
(ii) the deduction to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased;
and iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.
If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps: death case Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier) death case
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand) when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
Hence, in the considered view of this Tribunal, the income of the deceased is required to be assessed as per the minimum wages of an unskilled worker applicable in Uttar Pradesh, which were Rs.8278/- per month at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
31. The deceased can be considered a self-employed / on fixed salary, in absence of any documentary evidence to establish a permanent job or regular increase in income.
In view of the aforesaid, the deceased, who was aged 59 years and 10 months at the time of the accident, is entitled to an addition of 10% to his income towards future prospects in terms of the decision of the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court of India in the case, National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Sethi and Ors. (Supra) towards benefit of future prospects.
The insurance company has a contractual as well as statutory liability to indemnify the insured.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, issue no.1 is decided in favour of the petitioners.
Accordingly, one-half of the income of the deceased is liable to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.
(G). NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
35.
The date of accident is 03.11.2019.
Accordingly, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively towards loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is liable to be awarded.
Thus, claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.70,000/-
(40,000x+15,000+15,000) under this head.
36. Accordingly, the petitioner in the present case is held entitled to a total compensation of Rs.5,61,713/- (491,713+70,000) only.
The petitioner has been pursing the present claim petition since the year 2021.
Accordingly, the petitioner shall also be entitled to interest @ 7.5% per annum on the awarded amount from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.

38.
Therefore, respondent no.2 i.e. the National Insurance Company Ltd is held liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.
39. In view of above discussion, the respondent No. 2- insurer is directed to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
